A Sanskrit manuscript was obtained from the hand of the great <term>Chakravartin</term> <gloss>Universal Monarch</gloss> Chodrak Palzangpo. Based on his command to restore missing sections and translate the conclusion, the following parts were included:

In the tenth <term>bampo</term> <gloss>section or volume</gloss>, from the line stating, "It accomplishes all the purposes of activities," up to the line, "Perform the supreme recitation of the secret mantra."

In the twelfth <term>bampo</term>, from the line, "Blessed One, however, for the sake of a special purpose," up to the line, "The body of the <term>vidyadhara</term> <gloss>knowledge-holder</gloss> shall become radiant."

In the thirteenth <term>bampo</term>, from the line, "Merely hearing this ritual of the <term>mandala</term> <gloss>sacred circle</gloss>," up to the line, "One should carve it to the height of a man."

In the fourteenth <term>bampo</term>, from the line, "Having fully empowered the lotus, the water, and the white mustard seeds with recitations," up to the line, "One should wash with a white cloth seven times."

At the junction of the fourteenth and fifteenth <term>bampo</term>, from the line, "Eight silver incense burners," up to the line, "In all other various places, one performs all the activities as they are intended in the mind."

<summary>This page documents the editorial history of a Tantric manuscript, noting specific textual additions and translations commissioned by Chodrak Palzangpo to fill gaps in the tenth through fifteenth sections.</summary>
<keywords>Chodrak Palzangpo, bampo, Sanskrit manuscript, translation history, ritual instructions, mandala, mantra recitation</keywords>
